chapter: Decca years and the First Herd
title: Radio airtime and losing money at hotels
summary: The band was on Mutual radio from Roseland, and airtime later justified losing money at New York hotels to earn it back on the road.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. We were on radio right from the start, right at Roseland, when Mutual was a chain.

Those early days. But it really didn't take on any great effect for us or great coverage until the band became somewhat important via records, and then all of a sudden we started to get much better airtime and a lot more -- that's when we started playing major hotels in New York or wherever it was and if we had to lose $2,000 or $3,000 a week, it didn't matter because we were getting the right kind of airtime.
And then, when we left that engagement and went on the road, the money would come back. That was the way it was done in those days, with all the bands.
Because there were over 100 or more bands.
There was tremendous competition for this radio time.
Today it's a different kind of competition and different kinds of groups, but it's still competition.
